name: Botifarra
description: Botifarra is the most iconic card game of Catalonia, Spain. A point-trick partnership game related to Manille, it is played with a 48-card Spanish deck where the 9 (the 'Manille') is the highest trump. It is unique for its strict 'Obligatory Trumping' rules and its bidding system, where the dealer can choose the trump or delegate the choice to their partner ('Delegar'). The game is a staple of Catalan culture, combining rigorous strategic discipline with intense social rivalry.

history.origins: Originating in rural Catalonia in the 19th century, Botifarra evolved from the older game of Manille. Its name literally refers to a type of Catalan sausage, though in the game it denotes the 'Botifarra' (No Trump) contract.
timeline: 1800s: Manille variants become popular in North-Eastern Spain.
Early 1900s: Distinct Botifarra rules (delegating trump, doubling) stabilize.
1980s: Codification of regional tournament rules by Catalan associations.
Present: A symbol of Catalan national identity, played in every village and social club.
history.cultural: Played with extreme seriousness; many clubs forbid talking or signaling during play. It is an integral part of Catalan social life.
history.evolution: The game's complexity grew with the addition of 'Contrar' (doubling) and 'Recontrar' (redoubling) mechanics, which add a gambling layer to the strategic play.

setup.deck: 48 cards (1-12 in Coins, Cups, Swords, Batons). Ranking: 9 (Manille, 5 pts), Ace (4 pts), King (3 pts), Knight (2 pts), Jack (1 pt), then 12, 11, 10, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (0 pts).
setup.dealing: Deal all 48 cards clockwise (12 to each player).

rules.objective: Score more than 36 points (half of 72 total card points) in a deal. First team to reach a target (usually 101) wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Selection**: Dealer names a suit, No Trump ('Botifarra'), or delegates ('Delegar') to partner. 2. **Doubling**: Opponents can 'Contrar' to double the points. 3. **The Play**: Forehand leads. **Must Follow Suit**. If void, **Must Trump** if the opponent is winning the trick. 4. **Tricks**: Highest trump wins; else highest of led suit.
keyRules: Ranking is A-7-K-J-Q? No, in Botifarra: 9-A-K-Knight-Jack-others.
Jack of Trumps is NOT the boss; the 9 is.
The 'Botifarra' (No Trump) contract doubles the points of the deal automatically.

strategy.basic: Protect your 9s and Aces. Since the 9 is worth 5 points, capturing even one is a huge boost. Avoid leading trumps if you are weak.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Delegar' Logic: Only delegate to your partner if your hand is perfectly balanced with no strong suits. If you have five cards of one suit, always name it trumps yourself.
strategy.advanced: Managing the 'Contrar': Doubling is a psychological tool. Use it not just when you have trumps, but when you suspect the dealer delegated because they have a terrible hand.
tips: Track the 'Manilles' (the four 9s). If all four are out, the Aces become the bosses.
Always try to win the last trick; while it scores no bonus points, it often contains the final 'point' cards.

variations.name: Strict Trumping
variations.description: Standard tournament rules: you must always trump if void, even if your partner is currently winning the trick.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation clarifies tournament enforcement of mandatory trumping without changing engine parameters.

scoring.description: 72 points in the pack. Winners score the difference over 36, multiplied by any doubles.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 101 total match points.

synthesis.shortDescription: Catalonia's national card game. A rigorous partnership point-trick game where the 9 (Manille) reigns supreme. With complex trump delegation and strict over-trumping rules, Botifarra is a masterclass in strategic discipline and regional pride.
